Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the run-chase. It's a must-win game for England Women to keep the series alive. Maia Bouchier and Danni Wyatt-Hodge are in the middle, pursuing a mammoth score of 199. Megan Schutt has the ball in hand for Australia Women. Here we go!
…THE RUN CHASE…

Right then, the surface at the SCG looks pristine and England Women do have an explosive batting lineup but to gun down 199 is never easy, especially against a potent attack like the one Australia Women have. It should be a really watchable chase, so, don't go anywhere and join us for the run chase in a few minutes.

England Women conceded 300-plus runs in that final ODI and now, they have conceded almost 200 runs, putting immense pressure on the batting which has already been vulnerable. The pacers were sloppy at the start, bowling wides and hit-me deliveries but Lauren Bell did pick up an early wicket. The spinners couldn't really control the game the way they would have wanted and Sarah Glenn in particular was taken to the cleaners. They bowled and fielded well in patches but not for the entirety of the first innings.

After being put into bat first, Australia Women were quick off the blocks and the debutant Georgia Voll was impressive to begin with. However, she fell inside the Powerplay after which the pair of Beth Mooney and Phoebe Litchfield stitched together a fine stand worth 51 runs. Mooney held up one end and even hit some glorious boundaries on her way to 75 runs as the batters at the other end kept coming in and going hard at the bowlers. Tahlia McGrath was the most prolific with a cameo of 26 from just 9 balls as the Aussies almost breached the 200-run mark.

That is a massive batting display from Australia Women even without a couple of key batters and that just showcases their depth in all departments of the game. England Women need 199 runs for the win and it will be their equal highest run chase in T20Is if they get there.

A couple of runs to end the first innings and 15 runs come off the final over. Short of a length and around off, Georgia Wareham drags the pull wide of deep mid-wicket and races back for the second run. Australia Women finish with 198/7 on the board!

TOSS - England Women win the toss and will BOWL first.

Well then, the weather in Sydney has been a cause for concern in the last couple of weeks but the Sun is out and there's no threat of rain either and it should be an exciting contest. Can England Women make a comeback and give the Aussies something to think about? Or will Australia Women cruise to get another win? We shall find out. Toss and team news in a bit, so, stick around.

England Women on the other hand will be under a fair bit of pressure, having let go of opportunities in the ODI series and they now need to clean sweep the T20I series to have a chance of snatching the Ashes back. They do have a few changes in personnel from the ODI set up and the likes of Sarah Glenn and Freya Kemp might come straight into the XI.

Having sealed the ODI leg of the Ashes 3-0, the Aussies have 6 points on the board and a win here will be enough for them to retain the Ashes. Also, it is a similar set up in terms of the players and we might not see too many changes in personnel either. However, recent news have confirmed that skipper Alyssa Healy has been ruled out of the first T20I with a foot soreness which could be massive.

Hello and a very warm welcome to one and all. It is time for the T20I leg of the Women's Ashes to begin and Australia Women will be taking on England Women at the Sydney Cricket Ground for the first of three T20I matches.
... MATCH DAY ...

After an electrifying ODI series, the Women’s Ashes now shifts to the shortest format with the first of three T20Is set to unfold at the iconic SCG. It’s do-or-die for England Women, who must win every game from here to reclaim the coveted trophy. Australia Women, brimming with confidence, swept the ODI series 3-0. While they weren’t always flawless with the bat, their resilience stood out. Alyssa Healy’s classy half-century in the first ODI, Ellyse Perry’s match-saving knock in the second, and Ash Gardner’s stunning maiden ODI century in the third showcased their depth and determination. The Aussies have bolstered their squad with the addition of Grace Harris, bringing explosive power to their lineup. However, they’ll want more consistency from Beth Mooney, Phoebe Litchfield, and Tahlia McGrath. Their bowling attack remains formidable. Alana King was outstanding in the ODIs, weaving magic with her spin, and she’ll be key again alongside Georgia Wareham. Megan Schutt, Darcie Brown, and Kim Garth round out a lethal pace attack, and with home conditions in their favor, Australia will look to dominate. For England Women, it’s now or never. Trailing 6-0 in the Ashes, they must find a way to turn things around. Their batting has faltered, showing only flashes of brilliance. Heather Knight, the skipper, carries the burden of leading from the front. Natalie Sciver-Brunt, fresh off a half-century in the last ODI, will be crucial, while Danni Wyatt-Hodge, Alice Capsey, and Amy Jones need to deliver big. The inclusion of Dani Gibson, Bess Heath, Freya Kemp, and Linsey Smith adds depth and variety to the squad. England’s bowling has been their strength, with Sophie Ecclestone’s precision spin leading the charge. Linsey Smith offers support, while Lauren Bell and Lauren Filer will spearhead the pace attack. But for England to have any chance, their bowlers must be backed by the batters. Can England rise from the ashes and keep their hopes alive? Or will Australia seal the series in style and retain the trophy? The stage is set, and the SCG awaits a thrilling showdown!
